global_rules: Write as realistic internal enterprise documentation in Markdown, the way real teams write: headings, short paragraphs, some tables or lists, occasional informal tone in notes.
State every fact listed in must_state for the document clearly, using the exact numbers, names and IDs given.

Do not invent any other numbers, limits, dates, percentages, versions, team names, vendor names, regions or IDs beyond those listed for the document or in the shared context. Prose, rationale and context are encouraged; new hard facts are not.
Never state anything listed in forbidden_everywhere, not even approximately or by implication.
Each document starts with a metadata block: Document ID, Version, Title, Date, Status, and Supersedes or Superseded by where given.
Length target per document is given in approx_words. Do not pad with lists of invented facts; pad with realistic narrative, context, rationale and procedure.
Also never state anything in the document's own must_not_state list.
forbidden_everywhere: Any recovery tier, RPO or RTO for customer-service
Any termination or notice period for the PayNimbus contract
Any SLA, availability or response time for the LedgerOne integration
Any rate limit imposed by Relatia
Any budget or cost figure for the Kafka migration
Any version 1 of the shipping API, or a label generation target for it
Any maximum depth or size of the payment-retry queue
Whether payment-service calls PayNimbus synchronously or asynchronously
The Kafka topic name shipment-requests, or how shipping-service hands requests to carrier-gateway
The order in which order-service calls other services when placing an order
Which region hosts reporting-service, and which region is the disaster recovery region
The data warehouse name Polaris DW, or where reporting-service loads data
The egress-proxy component, or what sits between carrier-gateway and SwiftShip
Any date for a SOC 2 audit
Any cloud region names such as us-east or us-west

documents.title: Use RabbitMQ as the event bus
must_state: Decision: adopt RabbitMQ as the Orion event bus
Status: Superseded by ADR-019
Considered alternatives included Apache Kafka, rejected at the time because the team lacked operational experience

documents.title: Order API versioning and idempotency
must_state: Order API v2 introduces a mandatory Idempotency-Key header on order creation
Order API v1 will be deprecated once v2 is available
Motivation: client retries could create duplicate orders on v1

documents.title: Service to service authentication
must_state: All service to service calls inside Orion use OAuth2 client credentials issued by identity-service
Transport level security requirements for these calls are defined in POL-SEC-01 and are not repeated here
This applies to every internal call, including payment-service calling inventory-service

documents.title: Migrate the event bus to Apache Kafka
must_state: Decision: migrate the Orion event bus from RabbitMQ to Apache Kafka
Supersedes ADR-003
The order-events topic is created with 24 partitions
Topic retention follows the default in POL-DR-02 unless an ADR overrides it

documents.title: Retention for the order-events topic
must_state: Retention for the order-events Kafka topic is set to 14 days
This overrides the 7 day default in POL-DR-02 for order-events only; all other topics keep the default
Reason: reporting backfills after incidents needed more than a week of events

documents.title: Outbound limits for carrier-gateway
must_state: carrier-gateway outbound traffic to SwiftShip is capped at 100 requests per second
The cap deliberately stays below the contracted SwiftShip limit to leave headroom
A circuit breaker opens after 5 consecutive failures
Written as a follow up to postmortem PM-2025-014

documents.title: Order API v1
must_state: Order API v1 is deprecated
Sunset date: 2025-12-31; after this date v1 requests are rejected
v1 has no idempotency mechanism

documents.title: Order API v2
must_state: Order creation requires the Idempotency-Key header
Idempotency keys are retained for 24 hours; a reused key within that window returns the original order
Rate limit: 200 requests per minute per client
New integrations must use v2

documents.title: Shipping API v2
must_state: Shipping API v2 is served by shipping-service
Internal target for label generation latency: 2 seconds at p95

documents.title: PayNimbus integration
must_state: payment-service uses a 10 second timeout for PayNimbus calls
Status: Superseded by version v2

documents.title: PayNimbus integration
must_state: payment-service uses an 8 second timeout for PayNimbus calls
The timeout was reduced from 10 seconds to align with the PayNimbus contract response guarantee of 8 seconds at p99

documents.title: SwiftShip carrier services agreement
must_state: SwiftShip API rate limit: 50 requests per second
Vendor support hours: 06:00 to 22:00 Eastern Time

documents.title: SwiftShip agreement, Amendment 1
documents.supersedes: CT-SWIFT-2024 v1 for the terms below
must_state: Rate limit raised to 120 requests per second
Vendor support is now available 24x7
All other terms of the original agreement are unchanged

documents.title: PayNimbus payment services agreement
must_state: Availability SLA: 99.95%
Response guarantee: 8 seconds at p99
Settlement period: T+2
Fee dispute window: 60 days

documents.title: carrier-gateway incidents
must_state: Maximum retries per carrier request: 5
Escalate to the Logistics on-call

documents.title: carrier-gateway incidents
must_state: Maximum retries per carrier request: 3
Exponential backoff with a 2 second base
Retries were reduced after PM-2025-014
Escalate to the Logistics on-call; contact SwiftShip support within the contracted support hours

documents.title: Payment failures
must_state: Failed PayNimbus payments are placed on the payment-retry queue
payment-service processes the payment-retry queue hourly
PayNimbus has no secondary provider; there is no automatic failover

documents.title: Kafka consumer lag
must_state: Consumer lag alert threshold: 50,000 messages
The Kafka platform is owned by the Platform team

documents.title: Carrier label outage
must_state: Incident date: 2025-08-04
Root cause: a retry storm from carrier-gateway exceeded the SwiftShip rate limit, which was then 50 requests per second
Service affected: carrier-gateway
Follow ups: reduce retries in RB-CARRIER-01, and write an ADR to cap outbound traffic to SwiftShip (no ADR number assigned yet at the time of writing)

documents.title: Duplicate orders from v1 clients
must_state: Incident date: 2025-10-02
Root cause: clients still on Order API v1, which has no idempotency, retried timed out requests and created duplicate orders
Action: the Order API v1 sunset was accelerated and clients were told to move to v2 before the sunset

Tier 3 targets: RPO 24 hours
